slides.text: Dragons didn't go extinct; they just went to sleep. Disgusted by the greed of men, the ancient beasts buried themselves deep within the earth, their scales becoming mountain ranges, their fiery breath simmering into dormant volcanoes. I am a Listener, trained to press my ear to the soil and decipher the slow, rumbling heartbeats of the slumbering gods. For three centuries, my order has ensured their peace. Until the mining guilds brought their explosive machines to the Black Peaks.

I pleaded with the King, warning him that the Black Peaks were not mere stone, but the curled spine of Ignis, the eldest of the fire-drakes. The King only laughed, blinded by the promise of infinite gold. The digging commenced. Every blast of dynamite felt like a dagger in my own mind. On the seventh day of the excavation, the rhythmic, booming heartbeat beneath the earth suddenly stopped. A terrifying, absolute silence fell over the jagged mountains.

The miners cheered, thinking they had struck a hollow cavern. But I fell to my knees, weeping in sheer terror. Ignis hadn't died. The silence meant he was taking a deep breath. The ground shattered like glass. A colossal golden eye, glowing with the heat of a thousand suns, snapped open from the jagged rock face. As the sky turned to ash and the true mountains rose up to block out the sun, I whispered, 'Forgive us.'
